item.title: Council starts work to improve access to footways and cycle tracks in the city
item.description: Following an audit of Hull’s walking, wheeling and cycling network, and approval by Hull City Council’s West Area Committee, the local authority will soon start work in the west of the city to improve access controls to make it easier for people to travel actively around their local area. item.title: Santa is back at North Point Shopping Centre with a brand-new free grotto
item.description: North Point Shopping Centre has welcomed Santa back for 2025, and he’s got a brand-new home right in the middle of the atrium. item.title: Free exhibition opens next to one of Hull’s coolest coffee shops
item.description: A brand-new free exhibition space has opened inside The Monocle on Ferensway – and with Daze Coffee House right next door, it’s an ideal stop for anyone wanting a more interesting lunchtime break in Hull city centre. item.title: Popular cycle safety campaign returns with focus on schools
item.description: A successful cycle safety scheme will run across Hull for a fourth winter, but with a new focus on supporting young people who cycle to and from school to stay safe and stay seen during the darker nights. item.title: Three must-try board game spots in East Yorkshire we think you’ll love
item.description: Brew on Bond Street is a cosy café-bar right in Hull city centre at 76 Bond Street, HU1 3EN. Brew specialises in local craft beer, loose leaf tea and freshly ground coffee, with a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere that makes it a natural home for board game fans. item.title: New schools join walking and wheeling challenge to cap off successful first year
item.description: Three more Hull schools have joined a national challenge to encourage and support more children to walk and wheel to school in the city. item.title: Paralympian Roy Turnham leads vision impaired tennis taster days for Hull students
item.description: Hull-based Paralympian and blind athlete Roy Turnham has teamed up with Hull City Council’s Integrated Physical and Sensory Service (IPaSS) Vision Support Team to deliver two inspiring vision impaired (VI) tennis taster days for young people living with sight loss. item.description: Winter’s the perfect excuse to slow down a bit and find somewhere warm for a proper brew, a slice of cake, and a catch-up. item.title: Hull’s last remaining Scotch Derrick Crane returns home after restoration
item.description: Hull’s last remaining Scotch Derrick crane has been successfully restored and reinstated at the North End Shipyard, marking a major milestone in the city’s maritime heritage project. This iconic crane, a striking reminder of Hull’s rich shipbuilding history, has undergone extensive restoration thanks to funding from Hull City Council and The National Lottery Heritage Fund. […]
